paper.title: PACE: Two-Timescale Self-Evolution for Small Language Model Agents
paper.central_claim: A frozen small LM (4B-14B) can self-evolve its own agent without a stronger teacher by running prompt evolution first and, only after prompt gains saturate, proposing constrained control-logic (solver code) edits that are committed solely if they pass a held-out validation gate; this yields best accuracy on all 12 backbone-benchmark cells (up to +9.2% relative over vanilla in the abstract) and improves tau-bench pass^k.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to worker by claude-kimi; model type configured by controller (agent_model=haiku slot -> claude-sonnet-5-5[1m]).

sections_read: A.4 edit space and safety checks

evidence.quote: the SLM may propose constrained changes to safe-to-edit components of the agent pipeline, but a candidate structure is committed only if it improves over the current agent in a held-out validation while satisfying the resource budget
evidence.support_explanation: States the proposal/acceptance separation: SLM-proposed control-logic edits are committed only through a validation gate.

evidence.quote: prompt-space methods cannot directly repair structural bottlenecks such as brittle parsing, missing validation, or weak retry logic, and therefore often saturate once such failures dominate
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap of prompt-space optimizers (GEPA/MIPRO/ACE class).

evidence.locator: Sec 2 Related Work, PACE differs paragraph
evidence.quote: Self-referential code-evolution methods, in contrast, often allow structural changes throughout the search process, which can be unstable when the proposing model is small
evidence.support_explanation: Author-stated gap of code-evolution methods (Godel-Agent class) for small proposers; this is the premise, supported mainly by the paper's own Fig 1 on one backbone.

evidence.locator: Sec 3.3.2 Empirical Validation of Solver Updates
evidence.quote: samples a fresh subset from the training pool, varying both size and composition across iterations
evidence.support_explanation: The validation gate data is drawn from the training pool, so it is not disjoint from the data used for prompt-candidate evaluation and failure analysis.

evidence.quote: Validation subsets are not fixed: at each evaluation step, the agent dynamically samples a fresh subset from the training pool
evidence.support_explanation: Confirms 'validation' = dynamic subsets of the 200-example train split; the only fixed disjoint split is the test split.

evidence.quote: only for the final reported numbers. All experiments use seed
evidence.support_explanation: Test split is declared held out and used only for final numbers; the same sentence states a single seed (0), which conflicts with the 10-run claim in Sec 4.1.

evidence.quote: independent runs with different random seeds, and we report the mean accuracy in the main context
evidence.support_explanation: Main results are means over 10 runs; Table 6 reports std. Conflicts with 'seed 0' in E006 for at least the DSPy baselines.

evidence.quote: Mini-batch (50 samples) + test-set evals
evidence.support_explanation: The evolution-time token budget includes 'test-set evals', which leaves unclear whether the test split is touched during evolution (e.g., the post-commit full evaluation used for rollback).

evidence.quote: During evolution, validation uses single-trial evaluation on all tasks for efficiency; the final reported metrics use 4-trial evaluation
evidence.support_explanation: For tau-bench, evolution-time validation runs on all 115/50 tasks, the same tasks used for the reported pass^k; there is no held-out task set for the tau-bench case study.

evidence.quote: shows combining prompt and control-logic search is insufficient; the transition policy matters
evidence.support_explanation: Author interpretation of the epsilon=1.0 ablation (Qwen3.5-9B, MMLU and IFEval only; no variance reported in Table 3).

evidence.quote: PACE incurs a one-time evolution cost of approximately 2–3M generated tokens for Qwen3.5-9B, depending on the benchmark.
evidence.support_explanation: Reports evolution-time cost for PACE only.

evidence.quote: These results show that PACE trades additional inference-time compute for accuracy, and that the cost is concentrated in structural updates rather than prompt refinement.
evidence.support_explanation: Evolved solvers use ~3.6x-5.2x per-query tokens (App A.6); gains are therefore confounded with extra test-time compute unless a compute-matched baseline is given.

evidence.quote: Token counts in this section are estimates derived from code-level analysis of prompt templates, solver call patterns, and observed output lengths.
evidence.support_explanation: All cost figures are estimates, not metered usage.

evidence.quote: can trigger rollback if the full-evaluation delta is negative.
evidence.support_explanation: A committed solver edit can be rolled back after a later full evaluation.

evidence.quote: prompt-only evolution saturates, control-logic-first evolution is noisy, and PACE delays structural updates until prompt gains plateau
evidence.support_explanation: Trajectory claim for Fig 1 (one backbone, Qwen3.5-9B).

evidence.quote: Classify failures into structural categories, e.g., parsing errors, validation failures, retry failures, or inference-configuration issues
evidence.support_explanation: The proposer receives a failure taxonomy summary computed on the validation split (Alg. line 22 analyses failures on D_val), and the gate is then computed on a subset of the same D_val: proposal data and commit data overlap.

evidence.quote: Results should be interpreted as within-protocol comparisons rather than standard leaderboard scores.
evidence.support_explanation: Authors scope results to fixed controlled subsets (e.g., IFEval test n=141).

evidence.quote: we run prompt updates to convergence
evidence.support_explanation: +PE baseline is PACE's own inner loop run to convergence; isolates the contribution of the control-logic phase.

evidence.quote: the agent may modify control logic from the start, without a dedicated prompt optimization phase
evidence.support_explanation: +CE baseline isolates the effect of ordering; whether it uses the same validation gate is not stated.

evidence.quote: No stronger teacher model is used during evolution.
evidence.support_explanation: Proposer and executor are the same frozen SLM, matching the central claim of no frontier teacher.

evidence.quote: Nearly all rejected executable edits have non-positive validation gain
evidence.support_explanation: Table 4 counts proposed/executable/accepted/rejected edits (3 runs per task, 4B and 9B): the failure denominator for structural proposals is reported.

evidence.quote: PACE does not inflate variance despite its two-stage search
evidence.support_explanation: Std over multiple runs reported in Table 6; used for sigma-based arguments, but no significance test or CI.

evidence.quote: The only narrow cluster is Qwen3-4B HotpotQA, where all methods sit within one
evidence.support_explanation: Authors concede 'best on all 12 cells' includes a cell where PACE is within one sigma of Vanilla (0.776 vs 0.775).

evidence.quote: However, the accuracy gain on IFEval is substantially larger (+33.1 pp from +PE to +PACE)
evidence.support_explanation: Internally inconsistent with Table 1/10 (IFEval Qwen3.5-9B +PE 0.718 vs +PACE 0.761, +4.3 pp); abstract's 'up to +9.2%' also disagrees with Table 1 cells such as Ministral HotpotQA +29.8%. Reporting hygiene issue.

evidence.quote: We omit the CE-only baseline because multi-turn dialogue performance is highly sensitive to prompt quality
evidence.support_explanation: tau-bench has no CE-only or any external-optimizer baseline; only Vanilla vs +PE vs +PACE.

evidence.locator: App A.4 Safety constraints, validation gate
evidence.quote: deterministic validation samples
evidence.support_explanation: The implemented cheap A/B gate compares candidate and incumbent on 12 (number on the preceding line of the source) deterministic validation samples, versus Sec 3.3.2's 'fresh subset' and delta=0.02: with n=12 one example is 8.3 pp, so the gate is statistically very weak.

evidence.quote: Run a candidate comparison of two solver or prompt variants on the same sampled validation subset to verify whether a change improves accuracy.
evidence.support_explanation: action_compare_variants is the paired accept/reject instrument; no paired statistical test is applied.

evidence.quote: To validate this, we classify every failure on a 20-sample mini-batch into three categories
evidence.support_explanation: Failure-mode shift evidence (Fig 3) is based on a 20-sample mini-batch per benchmark, a small and noisy basis for the saturation premise.

evidence.quote: Gödel Agent, which permits structural modification, is more competitive but still trails PACE on most benchmarks.
evidence.support_explanation: Nearest structural-edit baseline is beaten on most cells; Godel Agent adaptation details to SLMs and its budget are not given.

evidence.quote: Across all SLM backbones, PACE achieves the best overall performance among the evaluated adaptation methods.
evidence.support_explanation: Headline result on four static benchmarks x three backbones (Table 1).

evidence.locator: App A.1 DSPy baselines / common protocol
evidence.quote: identical splits across Vanilla, +PE, +PACE, GEPA, and MIPROv2
evidence.support_explanation: Same splits used for all methods, but DSPy optimizers use the auto="medium" preset while PACE has 20 outer steps and 2-3M tokens; budgets are not matched or compared.

signatures.operation: Generate prompt candidates by handcrafted mutations, SLM-reflective revisions and crossover of complementary Pareto members; evaluate on train mini-batches

signatures.selection_rule: threshold on noisy dynamic validation subsets

gap.author_gap: Prompt-space optimizers saturate on structural bottlenecks; code-evolution methods are unstable when the proposer is a small LM; nothing coordinates the two for frozen SLMs.
gap.checked_gap: The gap is partly real and testable: prompt-only (+PE) vs control-logic-only (+CE) comparison shows complementary gains on several cells. The 'SLM-specific instability' premise rests on Fig 1 for one backbone and Table 4 proposal-rejection rates; the claim that structural-first search is worse is not shown across backbones/benchmarks.
gap.lineage: ancestors: DSPy-style prompt optimization (MIPROv2, GEPA) and playbook/context evolution (ACE); self-referential code agents (Godel Agent). PACE sits between them as a scheduler plus acceptance gate.
gap.closest_adjacent: Godel Agent (structural self-edit, baseline), ACE (context playbook), GEPA (reflective Pareto prompt evolution; PACE's inner loop closely resembles it). Other archive/validation-gated code-editing agents (ADAS/DGM-style) and harness-patching loops are not compared; nearest neighbors are not fixed as local sources, so adjacency is from reading only the paper's citations.
gap.residue: Fixed-schedule two-phase search with a threshold; commit gate with tiny/overlapping validation data; no retention across tasks.
gap.stakes: Frozen SLM agents under local serving constraints; structural bottlenecks (parsing/validation/repair) cap prompt-only gains.
gap.method_response: Delay structural edits until prompt gains saturate; commit only on A/B improvement with rollback; bounded edit space.
gap.remaining_gap: Whether staging and gating beat compute-matched hand-designed strategies; generalization of evolved solvers beyond the evolution distribution; statistical soundness of the commit rule.
unresolved: Matched-compute baseline (e.g., fixed self-consistency+PE) is absent.
Godel Agent/ACE adaptation to SLM backbones and their budgets are unspecified.

Sub-card C04 (compressing over-provisioned trained artifacts via sensitivity-based minority/bulk split) describes a different object and tactic, so no sub-card is assigned.

Success cond 'partition shown load-bearing by ablation' partial: PE-only and CE-only and eps/delta sweeps on one backbone. Failure 'treatment assembled from off-the-shelf modules' partly applies: inner loop resembles GEPA, gate is plain A/B.
matches.reason: Operation actually executed is a differentiated schedule over two distinct components of the agent, not just mentioning both; but the discriminating property is a scalar saturation trigger rather than a derived treatment.

rs_pattern.reason: Closest original card is heterogeneous_decomposition; no sub-card fits the harness-evolution object, so sub_id is null.
rs_pattern.resolves_problem: partial: improves over PE-only and CE-only on most cells, but 4B HotpotQA is a null result and the saturation premise is shown only on 20-sample batches.

matches.condition_checks: Inner loop is a prompt population with Pareto front and parent sampling by failure coverage; executable fitness is task accuracy on train mini-batches. rsi:population_search_executable_fitness/S2 (hard-to-game evaluator) met for deterministic benchmark metrics; F2 (re-skinned metaheuristic) is a risk since mutation/reflection/crossover resemble GEPA.

Control-logic phase patches executable solver code from a failure summary with bounded edit space and replay/rollback; but the proposer gets a compact failure summary, not full raw traces (S5 partial), and edits are not accompanied by falsifiable predictions. rsi:attribute_and_patch_incumbent/S3 (retention protects earlier wins) partial: only A/B gate and later rollback.

Propose/authorize separation present with fallback to incumbent; but H31 step 2 (split proposal data from commit data) is unmet: validation subset is drawn from the train pool and the same D_val feeds failure analysis; step 3 (statistic matched to noise) unmet with a 12-sample A/B and fixed margin.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS 'tailored operation for the prompt partition' = H13 prompt-population search with Pareto selection under fixed control logic.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: RS requires a derived discriminating property; here the partition is a design choice justified by a failure-mode shift observation.

pattern_mapping.operation_correspondence: RS 'tailored operation for the structural partition' = H12 scoped patch of harness code gated by replay/regression.
pattern_mapping.conditions_differences: H12 assumes raw traces plus source; PACE passes a failure summary. Edit scope is constrained by templates and immutable primitives.

claims.text: PACE is best on all 12 backbone-benchmark cells on four static benchmarks.
claims.setting: Qwen3-4B, Qwen3.5-9B, Ministral-3-14B; MMLU/MGSM/HotpotQA/IFEval fixed test subsets (800/800/500/141)
claims.baseline_control: Vanilla, MIPROv2, GEPA, ACE, Godel Agent, +CE, +PE
claims.selection_vs_test: train 200 + dynamic validation from train pool for selection; disjoint fixed test split for reporting (ambiguity: Table 9 lists 'test-set evals' during evolution)
claims.result_denominator: mean over 10 runs, std in Table 6; 4B HotpotQA is within one sigma of Vanilla (0.776 vs 0.775)
claims.counterevidence: No matched-compute control; baseline budgets differ; 4B HotpotQA null.
claims.allowed_conclusion: On these fixed subsets PACE's mean accuracy is highest in nearly all cells; for one cell it is not distinguishable from vanilla.

claims.text: Two-timescale ordering (prompt first, then gated structural edits) beats prompt-only, control-logic-only, and the naive combination.
claims.setting: Qwen3.5-9B MMLU and IFEval ablations; Table 1 comparisons
claims.result_denominator: ablations report single numbers (no std); main table has std
claims.counterevidence: Gate-off IFEval 72.3 vs PE 71.8 and CE 72.5 suggests the gate rather than the ordering explains most gain; IFEval n=141 so 1 item=0.7 pp.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Supported for one backbone on two benchmarks with small margins; ordering effect vs gate effect not cleanly separated.

claims.text: A frozen SLM can autonomously discover task-appropriate inference strategies, without a stronger teacher.
claims.setting: Evolved MMLU solver (3-way vote + verify) and IFEval solver (3 candidates + self-check + repair)
claims.baseline_control: none that fixes the same strategies by hand
claims.result_denominator: Table 4: executable proposals 21-46 per task over 3 runs, accepted 17-29
claims.counterevidence: Rediscovery of self-consistency is expected from the model's prior; compute multiplier of 3.6-5.2x is not controlled.
claims.allowed_conclusion: A 9B SLM can generate executable solver edits that pass an A/B gate; 'autonomous discovery' of superior strategy is not separated from simply spending more test-time compute.

claims.text: PACE improves multi-turn tool-use success on tau-bench Retail/Airline.
claims.setting: Qwen3-4B, Qwen3.5-9B; 115 and 50 tasks; Sonnet 4.5 user simulator
claims.selection_vs_test: validation on the same tasks as reporting
claims.counterevidence: No held-out tasks, no CE-only/external baselines, small Airline n=50.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Evolution on the evaluation tasks raises their pass^k; no generalization claim is supported.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On four fixed-subset static benchmarks and three small LMs, an evolved (prompt + gated solver-code) agent attains higher mean test accuracy than vanilla, prompt-only and control-logic-only evolution and the tested optimizers, at 1.6-5.2x per-query tokens; the retained agent is evaluated on a split disjoint from the dynamic validation pool (modulo the 'test-set evals' ambiguity).
assessment.cannot_claim: That staging rather than the gate or extra inference compute explains the gain; improver-level evidence; generalization of tau-bench results; reproduction (these are author reports, no our_run).
unresolved: Whether test-split evaluations occur during evolution (Table 9 'test-set evals').
Seed protocol contradiction (10 runs vs seed 0).

G.reason: Real, specific limitation (prompt saturation vs unstable SLM code edits) with named neighbors (GEPA, MIPROv2, ACE, Godel Agent); but the instability premise is shown on one backbone, other validation-gated code-editing agents are not compared, and PACE's inner loop is close to GEPA, so the residual bottleneck is only partly established.

M.reason: Operation chain is reconstructable (failure summary -> bounded solver edit -> A/B accept -> re-enter prompt tuning) and makes distinguishable predictions (epsilon extremes, gate-off) that are tested; assumptions on saturation threshold and failure-mode shift are thinly grounded (20-sample batches).

X.reason: Edit space, immutable primitives, syntax check, saturation gate, A/B gate, post-commit rollback and re-entry into prompt evolution are described in A.4/A.5; but gate data are drawn from the train pool and overlap with failure-analysis data (H31 step 2 unmet), the gate size is inconsistent (12 samples vs fresh subsets), and rejected candidates are not archived.

E.measurement.reason: Deterministic official metrics (MMLU letter match, MGSM numeric match, HotpotQA EM, IFEval strict checkers) and a fixed test split; tau-bench uses an LLM user simulator; subsets are small (IFEval n=141); cost metrics are estimates.

E.causality.reason: PE-only, CE-only, epsilon and delta sweeps and gate-off exist, but only on one backbone/two benchmarks without variance; no compute-matched fixed-strategy control although inference tokens rise 3.6-5.2x; baseline budgets (DSPy auto=medium, Godel Agent) are unmatched/unspecified; no store-off style test of the retained solver on a different distribution.

E.holdout.reason: Static benchmarks report on a disjoint fixed test split while selection uses dynamic subsets of the train pool, which is sound in intent; but Table 9 lists test-set evals in evolution, tau-bench selects and reports on the same tasks, and no transfer/cross-distribution test of evolved solvers is given.

E.statistics.reason: Std over 10 runs is reported for main results and a variance discussion exists, and proposal-rejection counts give a failure denominator; but ablations and tau-bench have no variance or CI, no significance tests, IFEval n=141, and the seed protocol is contradictory (10 runs vs seed 0).

E.cost.reason: Evolution cost (2-3M tokens) and per-query multipliers (1.6-5.2x) plus an accuracy-cost table are reported and the trade-off is acknowledged, but all are code-level estimates and baselines' costs are not reported, so no fairness comparison.

rationale: 两时标调度(先提示后受控制逻辑)+验证门,冻结SLM,静态基准测试集与选择集分离,10次均值。缺同算力固定策略对照,门控数据与故障分析重叠且仅12样本,tau-bench无留出。判定retained/scoped。
